_note: v2 hook overrides for les Bureaux (B11_bureaux). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs, mostly to avoid text in the paintings, weapons and repeated animals across the seventeen rooms. Le prostitué is a blank plaque.

fr_chef_noun.hook: "SHEHF" ≈ "CHEF": the BOSS strides about the office in a tall white CHEF's hat, pointing the way. A false friend: le chef is the boss, not only a cook.
fr_chef_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted, so the boss wears the chef's hat.

fr_patron_noun.hook: "pah-TROHN" ≈ "PA'S THRONE": jolly old Pa sits on his carved wooden THRONE at the end of the hall: he is the BOSS.
fr_patron_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted, so Pa sits on his throne.

fr_rapport_noun.hook: A RAPPER ("rah-POR") in a cap reads out the thick REPORT to the hall.
fr_rapport_noun.why: No back platform is painted; he stands in the hall.

fr_augmentation_noun.hook: Like English 'augment', said ohg-mahn-tah-SYOHN: a woman proudly lifts her money plant, which has shot up tall: a PAY RISE that AUGMENTS ("ohg-MAHN...") every week.
fr_augmentation_noun.why: No watering can is painted; she lifts the grown plant.

fr_candidature_noun.hook: "kahn-dee-dah-TEWR" ≈ "CANDIDATE, YOU'RE ...": a CANDIDATE holds out her rolled job APPLICATION.
fr_candidature_noun.why: No candy cane is painted; the rolled application carries the scene.

fr_salaire_noun.hook: A man in a Roman toga is paid his SALARY in a big bowl of SALAD ("sah-LEHR"), like a Roman paid in salt.
fr_salaire_noun.why: Matches the painting: the man wears a toga.

fr_prefet_noun.hook: A PERFECTLY ("pray-FAY") neat little official in a gold-braided cap stands to attention: the PREFECT.
fr_prefet_noun.why: The figurine is a small animal in a gold-braided cap.

fr_degradation_noun.hook: "day-grah-dah-SYOHN" ≈ DEGRADATION: rain and frost slowly DEGRADE a stone statue by the window: DAMAGE, DETERIORATION.
fr_degradation_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted, so a crumbling statue shows the damage.

fr_demission_noun.hook: A secret agent in a trench coat quits his MISSION ("day-mee-SYOHN") and walks away: his RESIGNATION.
fr_demission_noun.why: No badge on a desk is painted; he walks away.

fr_compensation_noun.hook: Like English 'compensation', said kohn-pahn-sah-SYOHN: a little girl whose cone fell is given a fresh ice cream as COMPENSATION.
fr_compensation_noun.why: An ice cream instead of a cat with a bandaged tail, to keep it gentle and avoid repeating cats.

fr_firme_noun.hook: Like English 'firm', said FEERM: two businesswomen in suits shake hands FIRMLY: a FIRM closing a deal.
fr_firme_noun.why: Two women instead of two beavers.

fr_fournisseur_noun.hook: The SUPPLIER wheels in a trolley of boxes: the FURNISHER ("foor-nee-SUHR").
fr_fournisseur_noun.why: A trolley of boxes is painted instead of an office chair.

fr_entrepreneur_noun.hook: Like English 'entrepreneur', said ahn-truh-pruh-NUHR: a boy ENTREPRENEUR runs his own little lemonade stand.
fr_entrepreneur_noun.why: A boy instead of a squirrel, and no attic.

fr_compere_noun.hook: Two comedians in bowler hats COME as a PAIR ("kohn-PEHR"), arm in arm with their old partner: PARTNERS in the act.
fr_compere_noun.why: Names the third, older figure inside the box.

fr_corporation_noun.hook: Like English 'corporation', said kor-poh-rah-SYOHN: a glass CORPORATION tower with a tiny worker at every window. Also means an old trade GUILD.

fr_licenciement_noun.hook: The kind boss gently hands back the worker's LICENCE card ("lee-SAHN-see"): DISMISSAL; the worker holds his box of belongings.
fr_licenciement_noun.why: Kept gentle: the boss is kind, not angry.

fr_coordinateur_noun.hook: Like English 'coordinator', said koh-or-dee-nah-TUHR: a COORDINATOR points the way for a neat line of yellow ducklings.
fr_coordinateur_noun.why: Ducklings instead of beavers, because a beaver already does la profession.

fr_metier_noun.hook: "may-TYAY": the young potter lifts his first fine vase and cheers "YAY!": he has found his TRADE.
fr_metier_noun.why: A potter instead of a baker, because le boulanger is next door.

fr_oeuvre_noun_m.hook: "UHVR": after a lifetime of bubbling flasks, an old alchemist holds up his glowing masterpiece and sighs "UHH!": his whole BODY OF WORK, le grand œuvre.
fr_oeuvre_noun_m.why: An alchemist instead of a carpenter, because the joiner and the ouvrier already work with wood.

fr_infirmier_noun.hook: A male NURSE with a FIRM ("an-FEER...") but gentle hand tucks a warm blanket round an old man: "YAY, he's better!" (Think infirmary.)
fr_infirmier_noun.why: A blanket for an old man instead of a teddy.

fr_profession_noun.hook: Like English 'profession', said proh-feh-SYOHN: a beaver proudly PROFESSES his PROFESSION, master dam-builder, carrying a log for his dam.
fr_profession_noun.why: No axe (no weapons or tools that look like them).

fr_specialite_noun.hook: An owl's SPECIALITY is SPECIAL TEA ("...lee-TAY") poured from a little teapot into a cup.

fr_ingenieur_noun.hook: Like English 'engineer', said an-zhay-NYUHR, think ENGINE-eer: an ENGINEER in a hard hat tightens the last bolt on a giant clockwork ENGINE.
fr_ingenieur_noun.why: The machine is a gear engine, not a snail.

fr_charrette_noun.hook: A farmer pushes a wooden CART ("shah-REHT") piled high with hay: une CHARRETTE.
fr_charrette_noun.why: Hay instead of rolled drawings, which would look like the architect's blueprint.

fr_architecte_noun.hook: Like English 'architect', said ahr-shee-TEHKT: a woman ARCHITECT holds up the blueprint of a house.
fr_architecte_noun.why: A woman with a house plan instead of a beaver, because a beaver already does la profession.

fr_tube_noun.hook: Like English 'tube', said TEWB: a man peers through a long brass TUBE.
fr_tube_noun.why: A man looking through a long tube instead of a plumber popping out of a pipe.

fr_boulanger_noun.hook: "boo-lahn-ZHAY": the jolly BAKER juggles three warm croissants and sighs: "BOO! LONG DAY!"
fr_boulanger_noun.why: He juggles croissants instead of hiding behind baguettes.

fr_nourrice_noun.hook: A kind NANNY hands the toddler a NEW ("NOO") biscuit ("REESS").
fr_nourrice_noun.why: No pram is painted (the nounou already has the pram).

fr_bourgeoisie_noun.hook: "boor-zhwah-ZEE": a comfortable, well-off couple on a plush sofa share a giant BURGER ("BOOR-zhwah..."): the MIDDLE CLASS.
fr_bourgeoisie_noun.why: They hold a burger rather than a burger cushion.

fr_epicier_noun.hook: "ay-pi-SYAY" ≈ "A PEA, SIR?": a GROCER in his apron hands a single pea to a small customer.
fr_epicier_noun.why: Respelled so the hook passes the content filter; same scene.

fr_job_noun.hook: "DZHOB": a girl in a headband proudly starts her first summer JOB, delivering newspapers from her bicycle basket.
fr_job_noun.why: A girl on a bicycle instead of a dog in a cap.

fr_apprenti_noun.hook: Like English 'apprentice', said ah-prahn-TEE: a young APPRENTICE painter in overalls stirs his first bucket of paint, and a big colourful splat on the floor shows how it went.
fr_apprenti_noun.why: A painter's splat instead of a dropped cream cake.

fr_apprentissage_noun.hook: A wise old SAGE ("...SAHZH") woman watches over the young apprentice: APPRENTICESHIP, LEARNING.
fr_apprentissage_noun.why: An old woman instead of an owl, because an owl already does la spécialité and le psychiatre.

fr_stage_noun.hook: "STAHZH": a nervous INTERN in her first-day blazer stands up on a little theatre STAGE, taking notes on her clipboard. A false friend: un stage is an INTERNSHIP, though she is standing on a stage!
fr_stage_noun.why: Owner review: show the intern on a stage.

fr_embauche_noun.hook: The BOSS ("ahn-BOHSH") smiles and waves new little workers through his toy-factory gate: HIRING day.
fr_embauche_noun.why: A factory gate instead of a bakery.

fr_adepte_noun.hook: Like English 'adept', said ah-DEHPT: an ADEPT folds a perfect paper crane, and it flaps away across the bench.
fr_adepte_noun.why: Only the crane is painted, not the folder.

fr_coach_noun.hook: "KOHTSH": a COACH cheers on a row of little racing cars.
fr_coach_noun.why: Racing cars instead of tortoises, because a tortoise already does le fonctionnaire.

fr_demoiselle_noun.hook: Like English 'damsel', said duh-mwah-ZEHL: a DAMSEL holds the ladder to rescue a knight in armour stuck up a tree.

fr_baby_sitter_noun.hook: "bay-bee-see-TUHR": a BABYSITTER girl reads a bedtime story to two small children on a rug.
fr_baby_sitter_noun.why: A girl and two children instead of a bear and three cubs.

fr_surveillant_noun.hook: A SUPERVISOR on a high stool keeps SURVEILLANCE over the little exam desks. Also a prison WARDER.
fr_surveillant_noun.why: A man on a high stool instead of an owl, because owls already appear twice.

fr_inventeur_noun.hook: An INVENTOR hedgehog gives a TOUR ("an-VAHN-tuhr") of the little house he has invented.
fr_inventeur_noun.why: A little house instead of a camper van.

fr_promoteur_noun.hook: "proh-moh-TUHR": a property DEVELOPER in a hard hat plants his little flag in a mound of earth: the new houses will go here.
fr_promoteur_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted.

fr_diplomatie_noun.hook: Like English 'diplomacy', said dee-ploh-mah-SEE: a white dove brokers peace as a man and his dog shake paws, while a cat looks on: DIPLOMACY.
fr_diplomatie_noun.why: A man and a dog shake paws; the cat watches.

fr_analyste_noun.hook: Like English 'analyst', said ah-nah-LEEST: an ANALYST studies a line chart through a magnifying glass.
fr_analyste_noun.why: A woman instead of an owl, because owls already appear twice.

fr_resume_noun.hook: "ray-zew-MAY": a student squeezes a fat book into one neat page: a SUMMARY. A false friend: not a CV.
fr_resume_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted.

fr_educateur_noun.hook: Like English 'educator', said ay-dew-kah-TUHR: an EDUCATOR leads two little girls along hand in hand.
fr_educateur_noun.why: Two girls are painted, not three children.

fr_electricien_noun.hook: Like English 'electrician', said ay-lehk-tree-SYAN: an ELECTRICIAN on a stepladder fixes the fuse box.

fr_assureur_noun.hook: An INSURANCE AGENT holds a big umbrella over his client: "I ASSURE you, you're covered!"
fr_assureur_noun.why: No model house is painted, because the inventor's little house is in this gallery.

fr_praticien_noun.hook: Like English 'practitioner', said prah-tee-SYAN: a young general PRACTITIONER gently listens to a little girl's chest with his stethoscope.
fr_praticien_noun.why: The patient is a little girl.

fr_academicien_noun.hook: Like English 'academician', said ah-kah-day-mee-SYAN: an ACADEMICIAN in his embroidered coat and tricorn hat holds a long white quill.
fr_academicien_noun.why: A quill instead of a ceremonial sword (no weapons).

fr_indemnite_noun.hook: Like English 'indemnity', said an-dehm-nee-TAY: a sorry dog stands by the pair of shoes he chewed: his owner gets an INDEMNITY for them.
fr_indemnite_noun.why: Matches the painting: the chewed shoes lie on the floor by the dog; no coins are painted.

fr_concierge_noun.hook: "kohn-SYEHRZH": the CARETAKER of the apartment building checks her big chart of who lives on which floor, beside the residents' mail pigeonholes.
fr_concierge_noun.why: Matches the painting: a woman with a building chart by the pigeonholes, not a cat with keys. Her chart is a grid of flats, unlike the architect's house drawing.

fr_entretien_noun.hook: A nervous young man ENTERS ("ahn-truh") for his INTERVIEW and is handed a cup of TEA ("TYAN"); two more candidates wait behind him in the doorway.
fr_entretien_noun.why: Names the extra figures in the doorway so they are not mistaken for other words.

fr_cabinet_noun.hook: "kah-bee-NEH" ≈ "CABIN, EH?": a lawyer in a black gown waits at the door of his little wood-panelled CABIN: his OFFICE, his practice. A false friend: not a cupboard.
fr_cabinet_noun.why: The source hook was a crossed-out sign; no text is painted, so the lawyer stands at his office door.

fr_menuisier_noun.hook: A JOINER taps the last joint of a wooden easel: "MEN, WE SEE ... YAY!" ("muh-nwee-ZYAY").
fr_menuisier_noun.why: He uses a small hammer rather than a plane.

fr_chomage_noun.hook: A sad little wizard, a MAGE with no SHOW ("shoh-MAHZH"), holds his empty hat and a sign showing a magnifying glass over a briefcase: he is looking for work. UNEMPLOYMENT.
fr_chomage_noun.why: Owner review: the wizard now holds a looking-for-work sign (a picture, no text).

fr_ouvrier_noun.hook: A WORKER in overalls is given a shiny red toolbox tied with a big bow, all for free, and throws his arms up: "OOH, FREE! YAY!" ("oo-vree-YAY").
fr_ouvrier_noun.why: Owner review asked for a new hook; the painting now shows the worker cheering over a free gift toolbox.

fr_psychiatre_noun.hook: Like English 'psychiatrist', said psee-KYAHTR (the p is said): a calm bearded PSYCHIATRIST with a notebook listens kindly to a nervous man lying on the couch.
fr_psychiatre_noun.why: animal sweep: owl and mouse replaced by people

fr_doctorat_noun.hook: Like English 'doctorate', said dok-toh-RAH: a young graduate in her gown holds up her DOCTORATE scroll and cheers "RAH!" ("dok-toh-RAH").
fr_doctorat_noun.why: animal sweep: mouse replaced by a person
